properties.name: record_alias — the one step of the five-step capture procedure that had nowhere to write
properties.rationale:
This is the one step of Anthony's five-step black-box capture procedure that had no surface under it. Measured 2026-09-08: steps 1-2 are the genesis interview, step 3's first half is capture-intent's 'search before you add', step 5 is the `undeclared_seam` detector and `seam_report`. Only 'update/annotate with new name' had nowhere to write — a sweep of all 28 node types found ZERO alias-like properties.

SO THE FIVE-ITEM WISH WAS A ONE-ITEM GAP, which is the whole reason this is small. Building the other four would have rebuilt what exists.

NO DETECTOR, DELIBERATELY. The three-legs doctrine asks for a typed tool, an instruction and a detector that notices absence — and the third leg is wrong here. A finding for 'this node has no alias' would fire on almost every node in every design and be correct nowhere: most nodes do not need a second name, and `req:detecting-is-not-asking` plus the history of hub-shaped detectors being cut back the week they shipped both argue against it. The instruction leg is served instead, in capture-intent where the capture actually happens.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether this removes the need for a translator. It gives the mapping a home; it does not choose a node type for a domain noun, which is the harder half and is still open in `dec:idea-a-users-domain-vocabulary-has-no-route-into-se-vocabulary`. Nobody has run the procedure on a live project.
properties.summary:
`aliases` (list:string) is declared on Requirement, Capability, Component, Interface and Flow, and `record_alias` writes it. An additive optional property, so the schema stamp does NOT move: 28 node types, 65 edge types, unchanged. Nothing needs migrating.

THE MERGE IS THE FEATURE. Terms are merged with what is already recorded, in the order they were learned, case-insensitively de-duplicated. Passing no terms is REFUSED rather than treated as a clear, because erasing somebody's vocabulary should not be reachable by passing nothing.

OBSERVED TO FAIL BY NEGATIVE CONTROL: replacing the merge with an assignment fails `recording_a_second_word_does_not_cost_the_first` and `the_same_word_recorded_twice_is_not_repeated`, while the other four cases stay green — so the tests pin the merge specifically rather than the feature generally.

SCOPE, STATED BECAUSE IT IS A JUDGEMENT: the five types name a THING in the user's world. Constraint and DesignRule are statements rather than things somebody has their own word for; an Artifact's name is the file's. The refusal for an unaccepted type names all five and says why.

THE INSTRUMENT NEEDED WIDENING TOO. `vocabulary_reach`'s tool-to-type map was tool → ONE type, and `record_alias` writes five. Mapping it to one would have left four reading as unreachable; leaving it unmapped would have pooled `aliases` across every type in the schema, which is the leak that map's own comment says it exists to stop. The map now accepts a tuple. Reachability still reads 0 HOLE.
